opportunities.title: Message Switch System Replacement
opportunities.description: The County of San Mateo (County) is seeking proposals from qualified vendors to replace its legacy Message Switch System (MSS), a mission-critical public safety platform that enables secure, real-time exchange of criminal justice information between local, state, and federal law enforcement systems. The Public Safety Communications (PSC) Department serves as the County's centralized emergency communications hub, providing 24/7 dispatch and emergency communication services for fire, emergency medical services (EMS), and law enforcement agencies serving approximately 800,000 residents throughout the County. The County's existing MSS supports approximately 30 law enforcement, public safety, and criminal justice agencies by providing secure connectivity to critical systems, including the California Law Enforcement Telecommunications System (CLETS), National Crime Information Center (NCIC), Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV), Automated Warrant System (AWS), County CJIS, and other criminal justice information systems. As the current platform has reached the end of its practical lifecycle, the County is seeking a modern, secure, scalable, and CJIS-compliant replacement that meets current operational needs while supporting regulatory compliance, interoperability, and future technology integration. The proposed solution will enhance system reliability, ensure uninterrupted access to critical criminal justice information, strengthen cybersecurity, and provide a sustainable platform that supports the County's long-term public safety mission.

opportunities.title: CHIP and CHA implementation, Governance, Community Engagement, and Data Integration Support
opportunities.description: San Mateo County Health, Public Health, Policy & Planning (County) seeks proposals from qualified consulting firms or organizations to provide specialized expertise in a time-limited capacity to provide advisory, facilitation, and capacity-building services supporting the County’s Community Health Improvement Plan (CHIP) and Community Health Assessment (CHA). The selected contractor will provide independent subject-matter expertise, structured facilitation, planning tools, technical consultation, coaching, and implementation-readiness recommendations. The work will help the County establish an effective CHIP/CHA governance structure; refine engagement approaches and implementation protocols; strengthen coordination with trusted-messenger community-based organizations (“CBOs”) and the CHIP backbone organization; and prepare the County to conduct comprehensive, equity-centered CHA/CHIP for future cycles. This procurement is for defined professional consulting deliverables. It is not intended to provide ongoing operational staffing, fill a County position, or delegate the County’s continuing public-health planning, program-management, data-governance, community-engagement, or policy-making responsibilities. The County will retain responsibility for the operational delivery of the CHA, including County decisions; community-engagement fieldwork; participant recruitment; survey administration; incentive administration; identifiable-data stewardship; language access services; final analysis and validation; and preparation, approval, and issuance of the final CHA/CHIP reports. Contract Structure Maximum contract amount: $85,000, not to exceed. Recommended contract term: 9–12 months, beginning after full execution of the County agreement. One contractor award is recommended. Compensation should be deliverable-based; payment is contingent on County review and acceptance of work products in accordance with the deliverable requirements and acceptance process described in this solicitation. No work may begin before the agreement is fully executed and the contractor receives authorization to proceed.

matched_keywords.description: The City of Pasadena Water and Power Department (“PWP”) is seeking proposals from qualified and experienced firms to provide wood pole inspection, repair, restoration, treatment, and related reporting services for PWP’s electric distribution system. The selected firm will support PWP’s ongoing maintenance and compliance program for wood poles, including visual inspections, intrusive inspections, groundline inspections, preservative treatments, minor corrective repairs, pole reinforcement recommendations, installation of approved repair materials, and detailed reporting of observed conditions. PWP’s wood pole program is intended to support safe, reliable, and compliant operation of the electric distribution system in accordance with applicable requirements, including California Public Utilities Commission (“CPUC”) General Order 95, Rules for Overhead Electric Line Construction, and CPUC General Order 165, Inspection Requirements for Electric Distribution and Transmission Facilities. PWP’s system includes approximately 11,000 wood poles, including both municipally owned and jointly owned poles. A significant portion of the pole population is located in rear property or otherwise constrained access locations. The scope of services may include, but is not limited to, pole condition assessment, identification of structural damage or decay, inspection for General Order 95 infractions, groundline and below-ground inspections, preservative and fumigant treatment, installation of visibility strips, guy guards, ground molding, pole tags, and steel truss reinforcement where approved by PWP. The selected firm shall also provide detailed inspection records, photographs, condition ratings, repair recommendations, and electronic data deliverables in a format acceptable to PWP. In addition to conventional field inspection and treatment services, PWP intends to include drone or other unmanned aerial vehicle (“UAV”) inspection services under the resulting contract. UAV services may be used to supplement field inspections, improve access to difficult or hazardous locations, document pole-top conditions, capture high-resolution imagery, and support more efficient assessment of pole attachments, crossarms, hardware, conductors, insulators, and other visible overhead facilities. UAV services shall be performed by qualified, FAA-compliant personnel and in accordance with all applicable federal, state, and local requirements. The selected firm shall furnish all supervision, labor, materials, equipment, vehicles, tools, technology, software, transportation, permits, methods, processes, and incidentals necessary to complete the work in accordance with the final scope of services, applicable laws and regulations, industry standards, and PWP requirements.

matched_keywords.title: Independent Medical Evaluation Services
matched_keywords.description: The City of Phoenix Retirement Office, on behalf of the Phoenix Fire Pension Board and the Phoenix Police Pension Board hereafter "Local Boards" or "Boards", through the City of Phoenix invite sealed offers from qualified contractor(s), including detailed information concerning qualifications and fees, to provide comprehensive disability medical record summary preparation and scheduling of independent medical/psychiatric examination services to the Local Boards. Arizona's Public Safety Personnel Retirement System (PSPRS) provides retirement benefits to police officers and fire fighters statewide, and the Local Boards are charged with benefit determination responsibilities for employees retiring from the respective City of Phoenix Departments. In a given year there are approximately seventy-five (75) disability benefit applications for which the Local Boards determine qualification and eligibility. The process starts with the presentation of a benefit application to the Retirement Office. Staff for the Local Boards then secures any relevant Worker's Compensation records and all medical information from the applicant's treating or examining health care providers. These records can be voluminous, particularly in circumstances where the development of an applicant's present condition is cumulative over an extended period of time. If records suggest that a benefit award is plausible, the Local Board's procedures mandate referral of the applicant and the records to an examination by a "medical board". That separate provider then renders a report on the applicant's condition, noting whether the condition meets the medical standards under the PSPRS statute. This Request for Proposal seeks services to compile and summarize the medical records gathered by Local Board staff in connection with each disability benefit application. Such a summary is expected to supply a clear, concise and chronological summary of the records that will enable the Local Boards to make their threshold determinations before referral to a medical board. The successful firm will also provide supplemental "ad hoc" services to the medical records services by maintaning panels of physicians or individual physicians capable of performing the independent examinations of applicants and scheduling appointments between qualified physicians and the applicant, as requested by Local Boards. The successful firm must serve as a single point of contact, ensuring coordinated scheduling, documentation, and communication with the Local Baords. Services include basic and ad-hoc evaluations, supplemental reports, and related administrative support to ensure accurate and compliant disability determinations. Agreement will be a five-year contract commencing on or about February 3, 2027, in accordance with the specifications and provisions contained herein, or the "Effective Date", which is upon award by Local Boards and appropriation by Phoenix City Council, conditioned upon signature and recording by the City Clerk's department, as required by the Phoenix Code, or whichever is later. Responses to this RFI are for informational and planning purposes only and do not obligate respondents to participate in any future procurement or take any other action. COH works countywide and collaborates with community-based organizations, public agencies, housing providers, and other stakeholders to strengthen the local homelessness response system. Family interim housing services are intended for households with children who are experiencing homelessness or a housing crisis and have no safe alternative housing options. In San Mateo County, these programs function as short-term, housing-focused interventions designed to provide a safe, decent, and family-appropriate place to stay while families stabilize, address immediate crises, and move as quickly as possible toward permanent housing. The County has not identified a specific region or facility for a new interim housing site. The County is seeking information from community-based organizations, shelter operators, housing and service providers, and other qualified entities with experience developing, establishing, and/or operating shelters or interim housing for families experiencing homelessness. opportunities.title: Wood Pole Inspection, Treatment, Repair, and UAV Inspection Services
opportunities.description: The City of Pasadena Water and Power Department (“PWP”) is seeking proposals from qualified and experienced firms to provide wood pole inspection, repair, restoration, treatment, and related reporting services for PWP’s electric distribution system. The selected firm will support PWP’s ongoing maintenance and compliance program for wood poles, including visual inspections, intrusive inspections, groundline inspections, preservative treatments, minor corrective repairs, pole reinforcement recommendations, installation of approved repair materials, and detailed reporting of observed conditions. PWP’s wood pole program is intended to support safe, reliable, and compliant operation of the electric distribution system in accordance with applicable requirements, including California Public Utilities Commission (“CPUC”) General Order 95, Rules for Overhead Electric Line Construction, and CPUC General Order 165, Inspection Requirements for Electric Distribution and Transmission Facilities. PWP’s system includes approximately 11,000 wood poles, including both municipally owned and jointly owned poles. A significant portion of the pole population is located in rear property or otherwise constrained access locations. The scope of services may include, but is not limited to, pole condition assessment, identification of structural damage or decay, inspection for General Order 95 infractions, groundline and below-ground inspections, preservative and fumigant treatment, installation of visibility strips, guy guards, ground molding, pole tags, and steel truss reinforcement where approved by PWP. The selected firm shall also provide detailed inspection records, photographs, condition ratings, repair recommendations, and electronic data deliverables in a format acceptable to PWP. In addition to conventional field inspection and treatment services, PWP intends to include drone or other unmanned aerial vehicle (“UAV”) inspection services under the resulting contract. UAV services may be used to supplement field inspections, improve access to difficult or hazardous locations, document pole-top conditions, capture high-resolution imagery, and support more efficient assessment of pole attachments, crossarms, hardware, conductors, insulators, and other visible overhead facilities. UAV services shall be performed by qualified, FAA-compliant personnel and in accordance with all applicable federal, state, and local requirements. The selected firm shall furnish all supervision, labor, materials, equipment, vehicles, tools, technology, software, transportation, permits, methods, processes, and incidentals necessary to complete the work in accordance with the final scope of services, applicable laws and regulations, industry standards, and PWP requirements.
